sentences.ko: 나도 그러고 싶은데, 너희 부모님이랑 하던 얘기 마저 해야 돼서.
sentences.text: I'd love to, but I got to get back to talking to your parents.

alts.text: Wish I could, but I gotta go finish chatting with your folks.
That sounds lovely, but I must return to my conversation with your parents.

sentences.note: **I'd love to, but** 는 제안을 부드럽게 거절할 때 쓰는 말이에요. **got to get back to** 는 하던 일로 돌아가야 한다는 뜻이라, 자리를 뜰 때 자연스럽게 써요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 내가 계산을 잘하는 건 아니지만, 여기 여자 셋에 남자 셋인 것 같은데.
sentences.text: I'm no math whiz, but I do believe there are three girls and three guys right here.

alts.text: Not great with numbers, but that's three girls and three guys, right?
Although I am not particularly good at math, I believe there are three women and three men here.

sentences.note: **I'm no math whiz, but** 은 '내가 전문가는 아니지만' 하면서 뻔한 사실을 농담처럼 짚을 때 써요. **I do believe** 는 do 를 넣어 '분명히 그런 것 같은데'라는 느낌을 살려요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아, 살면서 이렇게 불편했던 적은 처음이야.
sentences.text: Oh, I have never been so uncomfortable in my entire life.

alts.text: That was hands down the most awkward thing ever.
Never before have I felt this uncomfortable.

sentences.note: **I have never been so uncomfortable in my entire life** 는 '태어나서 이렇게 ~한 적이 없다'는 과장 표현이에요. 어색한 자리를 막 겪고 나서 친구에게 털어놓을 때 딱 맞아요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 8 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그리고 너 안 하면 다들 너한테 화낼 거야. 편이 안 맞잖아.
sentences.text: And if you don't play, everyone will be mad at you cuz the teams won't be even.

alts.text: Come on, if you sit out, the teams are uneven and everyone's gonna be mad.
Furthermore, if you do not participate, everyone will be upset with you because the teams will be uneven.

sentences.note: **the teams won't be even** 은 편 인원수가 안 맞는다는 말로, 게임이나 운동하면서 사람 수를 맞출 때 써요. **be mad at you** 는 '너한테 화나다'라는 뜻으로 일상에서 아주 자주 들어요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.text: It's a- It's this cute little place on 10th Street.

alts.text: Oh, cute little spot on 10th.
There is a charming little establishment on 10th Street.

sentences.note: **this cute little place** 는 작고 아기자기한 가게나 식당을 소개할 때 써요. 여기서 this 는 '이것'이 아니라 '어떤 데가 있는데' 하고 이야기를 꺼내는 말투예요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 무슨 문제인지는 몰라도, 너희 둘이 잘 풀 수 있을 거야.
sentences.text: Whatever the problem is, you can work it out.

alts.text: You guys'll figure it out, whatever it is.
I am sure that you will be able to resolve this, whatever the problem may be.

sentences.note: **work it out**은 다툼이나 문제를 대화로 풀어 해결한다는 말로, 싸운 친구나 커플을 달랠 때 자주 씁니다. **Whatever the problem is**로 시작하면 '사정은 모르지만'이라는 느낌이 납니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 누가 너보고 대장 하래? 왜 네가 다 정해?
sentences.text: I don't know who made you the boss.

alts.text: Since when are you in charge?
I do not recall anyone putting you in charge.

sentences.note: **who made you the boss**는 친구나 가족이 이래라저래라 할 때 '네가 뭔데 시켜?'라고 받아치는 말입니다. 비슷하게 **Since when are you in charge?**도 많이 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 괜히 차려입고 딴 사람인 척하는 거 말이야.
sentences.text: Dressing up and pretending to be someone you're not.

alts.text: Getting all dolled up and faking it.
Wearing formal clothes and acting as though you are a different person.

sentences.note: **pretending to be someone you're not**은 '본모습이 아닌 척한다'는 뜻으로, 소개팅이나 면접에서 꾸민 모습을 얘기할 때 딱 맞습니다. **dress up**은 평소보다 차려입는다는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 8 | Friends

sentences.ko: 어… 너 혹시 걔 화나게 한 거 있어?
sentences.text: Uh, did you do anything to make her mad?

alts.text: You piss her off or something?
Is it possible that you did something to upset her?

sentences.note: **make her mad**는 '화나게 하다'를 말할 때 angry보다 훨씬 흔하게 쓰는 표현입니다. 누가 갑자기 쌀쌀맞아졌을 때 친구에게 조심스럽게 물어보는 자리에서 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 걔 말로는 너네 연락 안 한 지 몇 년은 됐다던데.
sentences.text: Because she said you guys haven't talked in like years.

alts.text: She said you two haven't spoken in forever.
She mentioned that the two of you have not spoken for several years.

sentences.note: **haven't talked in years**는 '몇 년째 연락이 끊겼다'는 뜻으로, 사이가 멀어진 사람 얘기를 할 때 씁니다. 중간의 **like**는 '한' 정도의 어림을 넣는 말버릇이고, **in forever**도 같은 자리에 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends
